2 رمّضهُ , inf. n. تَرْمِيضٌ, (S, A, K,) originally signifies He attributed to him إِرْمَاض [meaning the causing one to be burnt by the heat of the sun, or by the vehemently-heated ground: or (assumed tropical:) the giving pain:] and hence, as this results from tardiness, (A, TA,) ―
-b2- (tropical:) He waited expecting him a while: (Ks, Jm, S, A, O:) or a little while, and then went away. (Sh, * K.) IF says that the م may be original, or it may be a substitute for ب. (TA.) ―
-b3- رمّض الغَنَمَ: see رَمَضَ. ＝
-A2- رَمَّضْتُ الصَّوْمَ I purposed fasting or the fast [app. during the month of رَمَضَان]. (Sgh, K.)
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
